name: Long-Term Residence Permit (Uzun Dönem İkamet İzni)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 8 years of continuous legal residence on a permit (student-permit time counts at half rate).
This requires sufficient and stable income, no social assistance received in the past 3 years, valid health insurance, and no public-order/public-security threat.

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: absence from Turkey exceeding 1 continuous year (except for health/education/compulsory public service) can result in cancellation

sources.title: Long-Term Residence Permit - Presidency of Migration Management

notes: Turkey's genuine PR-hub route, holding indefinitely once granted and treated as equivalent to Turkish citizens for most purposes EXCEPT voting, being elected, public-service employment, compulsory military service, and vehicle-import customs exemptions — a real, specific, and generous set of rights short of citizenship worth flagging as one of the most substantively 'citizenship-adjacent' non-citizen statuses in this entire multi-country dataset. Refugees, conditional refugees, subsidiary-protection beneficiaries, temporary-protection holders, and other humanitarian-status holders are EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED from transferring to this route — a genuine and consequential structural exclusion, distinct from most other countries' asylum-to-PR pathways in this dataset, which typically DO allow protected persons to reach settlement status eventually. Re-applications after cancellation do not require the 8 years again and are prioritised — a real mitigating mechanic worth noting. citizenship_after_months (0) reflects that Turkey's naturalisation clock (5 years) runs INDEPENDENTLY of this route rather than being gated behind it — someone could naturalise via tr_ordinary_naturalisation without ever holding this status at all, the same structural pattern already flagged on Japan's naturalisation route in this dataset.
